pc.file: Point cloud or scan file (LAS, LAZ, E57, PLY, OBJ, USDZ, PCD, PTX, XYZ or PTS)
pc.err.no_app: Open a model first: the cloud is drawn in the app's 3D view, which the app makes with the first model.
pc.err.no_3d: The app's 3D view is not available yet. Open the 3D view and try again.
pcx.note.bim: Drawn in BimCraft's 3D view beside the model. LAS, LAZ and E57 are read in pieces and tiled with every point; PLY, PCD, PTX, XYZ and PTS are read by the app's own reader (at most 3 million points kept, thinned evenly) and then tiled the same way. Metres are assumed unless the file says feet. Eye-dome lighting starts off here.
pcx.note.cad: Drawn in CadCraft's 3D tab. LAS, LAZ and E57 are read in pieces and tiled with every point; PLY, PCD, PTX, XYZ and PTS are read by the app's own reader (at most 3 million points kept, thinned evenly) and then tiled the same way. Metres are assumed unless the file says feet. The ground and class tools are not in this app. Eye-dome lighting starts off here.
pcx.thinned: The file has {read} points; {kept} were kept, spread evenly, before tiling.
pcx.e57.full: E57 file read page by page: all {n} points kept, none thinned.
pcx.cmp.title: Compare with model
pcx.cmp.what: Measures how far each scan point is from the nearest surface of the model's elements, colours the points by that distance and lists every element: within the tolerance, outside it, only partly scanned, or not scanned at all. The scan is taken as placed in the 3D view; a scan that is shifted or at the wrong scale shows large distances everywhere, so check scale and level first.
pcx.cmp.verify: Mark the {n} elements within tolerance as field-verified
pcx.cmp.nomodel: Open a model with elements in the 3D view first: there is nothing to compare the scan with.
pcx.cmp.summary: {tested} points tested against the model, {unmatched} of them farther than the search distance from every element. Elements: {within} within {tol} mm, {outside} outside, {partial} only partly scanned, {unseen} not scanned.
pcx.cmp.band.beyond: over {mm} mm, or not near any element
pcx.cmp.col.name: Element
pcx.cmp.more: {n} more elements are in the CSV report.
pcx.cmp.vnote: Compared with a scan: mean distance within {tol} mm of the model.
pcx.cmp.basis.model: from the size of the model
pcx.cmp.basis.size: from the size of the scan alone
pcx.cmp.n.unit: The scan looks like it is in {unit} ({pct} % sure, {basis}). Open it again with that unit.
pcx.cmp.n.up: Its layers say {axis} is up, not Z. A phone scan is often Y up.
pcx.cmp.n.tilt: The floor leans {deg} degrees. Level it before comparing.
pcx.cmp.n.nofloor: No floor was found: there is no large flat layer to level by.
pcx.cmp.n.size: The scan is about {m} m across, which is unusual for a building.
pcx.cmp.n.ok: Scale, up axis and level look right.
pcx.cmp.n.height: Height between the floor and the next layer above it: {m} m.
pcx.mesh.note: Read as a mesh: {n} points laid on its surface about every {mm} mm.
pcx.mesh.up: Turned from {axis} up to Z up and levelled by {deg} degrees.
pcx.mesh.usdc: This USDZ holds a binary USD file, which is not read yet. Export OBJ or PLY from the scanning app instead.
pcx.mesh.unit: The scan looks like it is in {unit}; metres are assumed. Set the unit when you open it if that is wrong.
pc.err.usdc_unsupported: This USDZ holds a binary USD file, which is not read yet. Export OBJ or PLY from the scanning app instead.
pc.err.mesh_no_points: The file holds no surface or points that could be read.
pc.err.ply_header: This is not a PLY file, or its header is cut off.
pc.err.ply_format: This PLY uses a format that is not read (only ascii and binary).
pc.err.ply_no_vertices: The PLY file has no vertices.
pc.err.ply_no_xyz: The PLY file's vertices have no x, y and z.
pc.err.ply_type: The PLY file uses a number type that is not read.
pc.err.ply_truncated: The PLY file ends before its data does.
pc.err.obj_no_vertices: The OBJ file has no vertices.
pc.err.zip_not_zip: This USDZ is not a valid archive.
pcx.mesh.upunclear: The scan's layers suggest {axis} may be up, but that is not certain, so it was left as it is. Check it in the 3D view.
